content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4: move cross-skilled agents, cancel payments coaching, add chat deflection and IVR callback. Predicted 77.2% service level for 16:15-20:00, short of the 80% target, at ₹1,347 extra.","why":"Payments demand jumped after the 10:55 reward-points email to 500,000 card holders. Calls reached +52% at 11:30 (164 vs 108 expected) and service level fell to 32%. The extra calls are mostly generic reasons: other_payments (1.77x normal) and refund_status (1.56x). Confidence in the cause is medium, because the email is about card rewards rather than clearly Payments & UPI. With no action, service level over 16:15-20:00 is predicted at 69.3%, with payments at 59.5%. P4 is the best plan that stays within policy. It lifts service level to 77.2% (payments 71.7%) and cuts abandons from 9.3% to 6.4%. No compliant plan reaches 80%.","trade_offs":["Cost: P4 costs ₹1,347, the same as P3 and R1, and gives the best result of the three. P3 reaches 76.4%, R1 only 75.1% despite its bigger agent moves. The cheaper staffing-only options (P1, P2: ₹75) barely help, at 70.2% and 69.5%.","General queue: moving agents drops general from 94.4% to 90.2%, still comfortably healthy. R1's larger moves push general down to 88.8% and do worse overall.","Customer impact: chat deflection and callbacks steer some refund/payment-status callers away from waiting on the phone line, which helps cut abandons to 6.4%.","R2 would reach 85.3%, but its known-issue IVR message breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident, so it is not recommended."],"watch":"Payments will still be below the 80% target, so keep an eye on payments service level and abandons, especially in the 17:00-18:00 peak when 6 agents are moved. Check that general stays near 90%. If the extra calls turn out not to be about Payments & UPI, re-check the plan."}
